headline: I started a local club to discuss European politics and now my neighborhood association requires a 400-page manifesto to hold a barbecue
body:
It was supposed to be a casual Sunday gathering. I foolishly thought that after spending six months deep-diving into the nuances of European parliamentary shifts—specifically the recent surge of the Alternative for Germany—I could host a small backyard get-together to share my findings with the neighbors. I didn't realize that by mentioning 'electoral realignment' over a plate of samosas, I had triggered the local homeowners' association’s automated Governance Protocol.

By Tuesday, I had received a registered notice stating that any social function involving more than three participants must now be preceded by a formal policy proposal. I am currently staring at a requirement to draft a 400-page manifesto, complete with a five-year fiscal projection and a detailed stance on every continental border issue, just to justify my plans for a Friday night grill-up. The HOA board insists that since I showed an interest in 'large-scale political shifts,' I am now legally obligated to manage my social life with the same level of bureaucratic rigor as a regional legislative body.

I tried to explain that I just wanted to eat chicken tikka with the guy from 4B, but the board secretary simply reminded me that my 'demonstrated appetite for political complexity' makes me uniquely qualified to fill out the mandatory 82-part 'Public Assembly and Ideological Impact' form. I haven't even fired up the charcoal, and I've already had to submit three separate impact assessments regarding the potential ideological drift of our cul-de-sac. If I have to draft one more annex on municipal zoning for an outdoor gazebo, I think I’ll just move to the woods.
caption: My neighbor tried to talk politics at a BBQ and now we all need a permit for a burger. Governance has gone fully meta. #LocalPolitics #BBQBlues #Bureaucracy #TooMuchDetail (satire)
